chunks: 8 - He said: Abu 'Ubayd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Marzubani informed me, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Mahran narrated to us, he said: Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Wahid, from Isma'il ibn Rashid, from Hudhlam ibn Satir who said: I arrived in Kufa in Muharram of the year sixty-one, at the time of the return of 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, with the women from Karbala, and with them were soldiers surrounding them.

The people had come out to look at them. When they brought them on camels without saddles, the women of Kufa began weeping and wailing. Then I heard 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, saying in a feeble voice, exhausted by illness, with the iron collar on his neck and his hand shackled to his neck: Indeed! These women are weeping, so who killed us? He said: And I saw Zainab daughter of 'Ali, peace be upon them both, and never had I seen a modest woman more eloquent than her, as if she was pouring forth from the tongue of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. He said: She had gestured to the people to be silent, and the breaths were held back and the voices fell silent.

Then she said: All praise be to Allah and blessings upon my father, the Messenger of Allah. Now then, O people of Kufa, O people of treachery and betrayal! May your tears never cease and may your wailing never subside! Your likeness is nothing but "like she who unraveled her yarn after having spun it strongly into strands, taking your oaths as a means of deceit among yourselves." Indeed, is there among you anything but arrogance and filth, and hearts full of rancor?

Cowards in battle, helpless against enemies, breakers of allegiance, wasters of trust! How wretched is that which your souls have sent forth for yourselves, that the wrath of Allah fell upon you, and in the punishment you shall abide forever.
Do you weep?! Yes, by Allah, weep much and laugh little, for indeed you have won its shame and its disgrace, and you will never wash away its stain from yourselves ever.

For the descendant of the Seal of Prophethood, the Master of the youth of Paradise, the refuge of your best, the resort of your calamities, the sign of your guidance, and the path of your proof -- you abandoned, and him you killed?! Indeed, evil is that which you bring upon yourselves! So perdition and reversal! For indeed the endeavor has failed, the hands are ruined, the bargain is lost, you have returned with the wrath of Allah, and humiliation and wretchedness have been struck upon you. Woe to you! Do you know which liver of Muhammad you have torn, which blood of his you have shed, and which noble woman of his you have violated? "Certainly you have brought a monstrous thing, whereby the heavens would almost split asunder, the earth would split open, and the mountains would crumble in ruins," and indeed you have committed a reckless, hideous act filling the earth and the sky.

Are you surprised that the sky rained blood?! And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful. So let not the respite beguile you, for indeed He is not hastened by urgency, and He does not fear the loss of vengeance. Nay! Verily your Lord is ever watchful. He said: Then she fell silent, and I saw the people bewildered, having put their hands in their mouths. And I saw an old man who had wept until his beard became wet, and he was saying: Their elders are the best of elders, and their progeny, when progeny is counted, does not disappoint and does not bring shame.
ai.seo_question: What did Zainab bint Ali say in her sermon at Kufa after the Battle of Karbala?
ai.summary: This is the famous sermon of Zainab bint 'Ali (peace be upon them) delivered at Kufa in Muharram 61 AH, after the tragedy of Karbala. As the captive family of Imam al-Husayn was paraded through Kufa, Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) first rebuked the weeping Kufans by asking who had killed them. Then Zainab, described by the eyewitness Hudhlam ibn Satir as more eloquent than any modest woman he had ever seen -- as if speaking with the tongue of her father Imam 'Ali -- silenced the crowd and delivered a searing address. She condemned the Kufans for their treachery, comparing them to the Qur'anic woman who unraveled her yarn (16:92), and enumerated their moral failures. She reminded them that they had abandoned and killed the grandson of the Prophet, the Master of the youth of Paradise. Quoting the Qur'an (19:89-90), she declared their deed so monstrous that the heavens nearly split. She warned them not to be deceived by divine respite, for Allah is ever watchful (89:14). The crowd was left stunned, with an old man weeping and reciting poetry praising the noble lineage of the Prophet's family.
